metadata.title: Gamut mask tool for miniature painting - PlaySupport
metadata.description: Easily make a harmonious miniature painting palette with a gamut mask tool.
metadata.ogTitle: Gamut mask tool for miniature painting
metadata.ogDescription: Easily make a nice, harmonious color palette for your miniature painting project.

GamutPage.title: Gamut mask tool for miniature painting
GamutPage.intro: Create a harmonious miniature painting palette! Place at least 3 colors to define a color-scheme mask, and explore estimated paint mixes below.
GamutPage.wheelAria: Interactive color wheel. Click to add a paint, drag to move it, double click or right click to remove it.
GamutPage.wheelHint: Click the wheel to add a paint · drag to move · double-click or right-click to remove
GamutPage.needPoints: Add at least 3 points that do not lie on a straight line to form a gamut mask.
GamutPage.valueHint: You can slide down for shadows where you will find browns and up for highlights
GamutPage.noPaints: No paints yet — click the wheel to add one.
GamutPage.exportError: Could not create the PDF. Please try again.
GamutPage.printHint: The PDF uses approximate, unprofiled CMYK. Printed colors vary with the printer, paper and ink and may differ from both your screen and physical paints.
GamutPage.mixesHint: These previews estimate mixes between neighboring mask points. Real paints depend on their pigments and may produce different results.
GamutPage.triangleHint: This triangle simulates actual paint pigment mixing behaviour.
GamutPage.triangleAria: Estimated three-paint mixing triangle. Numbered corners correspond to the selected paints.
GamutPage.triangleUpdating: The mixing triangle updates when you finish dragging.
GamutPage.manyPaintsHint: With more than three paints, there are more mixing combinations than a flat polygon can show. The previews below estimate mixes between neighboring mask points instead.
GamutPage.aboutText: A gamut mask is a simple way to pick your colors so that you get a nice color scheme for your miniatures or paintings! It was originally created by James Gurney.
GamutPage.maskText: To make a gamut mask, pick 3 or more points on the color wheel. The shape helps you choose a color scheme, but its HSL colors are not guaranteed paint mixtures. Use the mixing previews to explore estimated mixes.
GamutPage.valueText: Color science is a bit complicated, so we also have the value (lightness) slider. You can find shadow colors by dragging it down, your saturated main colors by keeping it in the middle, and your highlights by dragging it up. I suggest first making a midtone shape and then dragging the value slider down to see what kind of dark colors you can add to your palette while maintaining perfect color harmony. Drag it up to see what kind of off-whites you could use for highlights, or just mix in your white. This will give you a very similar effect to GW's Tone Triads or Army Painter's triads.
GamutPage.paletteText: In miniature painting, we don't like to use only 3 colors plus black and white, but rather many different colors so we don't have to mix all the time. However, this can make our paint schemes less interesting and less visually moody or striking than mixing them from fewer colors. By checking what colors are inside your shape and comparing them to paints you already have or could get for your paint scheme, you can have the best of both worlds.
